prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer standing at an indoor doorway threshold with a stove and wall partition within arm's reach on the left (about 0.3–0.6 m away) and the wearer's own right hand holding a small food piece at roughly 0.3–0.5 m on the right, opening into a living room extending 2–4.5 m ahead. In the living room, an armchair edge sits on the left (~1.8 m), a dog sits on the floor in front (~0.8–1.2 m), a TV rests on two wooden crates to the right (~2.2–2.8 m, about 1–1.5 m behind the dog), and a brown mattress lies against the back wall (~3.5–4.5 m). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer tilts and shifts slightly right while raising their right arm from the lower right to the upper right above the dog, as the dog rises and moves closer from partially out of view at the bottom edge (frames 1–3) to ~0.7–1.0 m directly below the raised hand (frames 4–5), partially occluding the left wooden crate. The depth map clarifies the continuous floor gradient and sharp depth discontinuities between the foreground doorway/stove, the mid-ground dog and crates, and the far wall that are less explicit in the wide-angle RGB image. However, it is unreliable in the far background (over-darkening the mattress and back wall beyond 3.5 m into uniform black) and flattens the raised forearm and hand into uniform saturation without fine finger or burner surface detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground regions across the scene, though no other people besides the camera wearer are present (only the wearer's right hand and arm at ~0.3–0.5 m and a dog at ~0.7–1.2 m facing and looking up toward the raised hand). In frames 1–3, the wearer's hand is in the lower right within arm's reach, while in frames 4–5 the arm extends upward on the right above the rising dog, which sits ~1–1.5 m in front of the TV (~2.2–2.8 m away) and partially occludes the wooden crate beneath the TV in frame 5. The map provides sharp pixel boundaries for the wearer's hand/arm, the emerging dog in frames 4–5, and the distant TV screen across frames 2–5, separating them from the cluttered background. However, it is highly unreliable and temporally inconsistent: it mislabels the left-side stove (~0.3–0.6 m, partially out of view on the left and receding by frame 5) as a 'refrigerator' in frame 1, misses it entirely in frames 2, 4, and 5, and labels it 'oven' only in frame 3. It also misclassifies the dog's head at the bottom edge of frame 3 as a 'person', mislabels the occluded wooden crate as 'book' in frame 5, and fails to segment the background mattress, armchair, crates, and walls.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's raised right hand in the upper right of frame 4 (~0.4–0.5 m from the camera). In context with the RGB strip, no other people are in the room—only the camera wearer (whose body is out of view behind the camera) and a dog sitting ~0.7–1.2 m in front, looking upward toward the wearer's hand as the hand rises from the lower right (frames 1–3) to the upper right (frames 4–5) within arm's reach above the dog. In frame 4, the magenta keypoints explicitly show the 3D finger articulation and downward-pinching orientation of the wearer's hand holding the small item, which is partially self-occluded in the RGB view. The map is unreliable in frames 1–3 and 5, where it completely misses the wearer's visible right hand and forearm at the bottom and upper edges of the frame. Because the pose estimator only tracks human skeletons, it provides no spatial information about the dog, the adjacent stove on the left (~0.3–0.6 m), or the room furniture 2–4.5 m behind the dog.
